LM.ranking_note: Inner lists are ties. C covers scan 483 only and is ranked on that page (no errors there, as A, B, E, G and H).

characters.A: Complete, literal and careful: every mark stays where it stands, and his loose syntax is kept (the doubled "that", the subjunctive "be the one induced"). Its one slip is the calque "effective action", which an English reader may take for "faithful action".
characters.B: Complete and generally faithful, with every mark present and his abbreviations written out. It turns the subjunctive "soit" into "is", widens one \unsure to take in "apart", and has three calques ("effective action", "a part I'", "conjectural optic").
characters.C: Covers scan 483 only; there it is error-free, keeps every mark, and even keeps the French order of the qualifiers ("curves geometrically connected (for convenience), anabelian"). One page says nothing about the dense deleted and inserted passages of scans 485-487.
characters.D: Fluent but the least careful version: it drops three marks (a \deleted{\illegible{1}} and two \unsure), moves words across the scan-484 anchor and into an insertion, widens an \unsure, changes \mathrm{Centre} to \mathrm{Center} and leaves \text{ou} in French. It also smooths what the brief says to keep (the doubled "que", the subjunctive "soit", the emphatic "bien"), turns "on" into "I" once, and leaves "rat" and "arithmet." unexpanded.
characters.E: Complete and faithful, every mark in place, subjunctives and doubled "that" kept. Two English stumbles: "effective action" and "do come all of them from".
characters.F: Faithful and the most idiomatic of the full versions ("an actual action", "rid ourselves", "This does not thereby mean"), all marks kept. It moves "necessarily" back across the scan-484 anchor and has one awkward "do come all from".
characters.G: Complete and faithful, every mark in place, the emphatic "bien" well rendered ("indeed all come"). Two English stumbles: "effective action" and "not only they commute".
characters.H: The most literal about marks: every mark stays exactly where it stands in the French, and it gets "an actual action" right. The cost is two non-English word orders where an insertion follows its noun (a subgroup "open" E', the homomorphisms "admissible" of the ...).

LM.conclusion: No version makes a major error on these pages, and the differences among A, E, F, G and H do not matter to a reader of an edition: each has one or two minor slips (a calque, an awkward order, one word displaced across a page anchor) that a copy-edit catches, and all keep the deletions, insertions, doubts and his loose syntax. B is a step down (a smoothed subjunctive, a widened doubt, three calques). D is the only version whose errors would mislead a reader about the manuscript: it loses and displaces marks, changes a formula and smooths his syntax. Five of the seven full versions write "effective action" for "action effective"; only F and H write "actual action".

characters.A: The most accurate and idiomatic version: it keeps the editors' brackets, the [sic] "right adjoint", the redundant "in addition ... in addition", the elliptic "`f_*` an equivalence" and the subjunctive "which would have", with apt English ("the prime", "the right-hand side", "Evidently"). Its one slip, shared by every full version, is "no doubt" for the hedge "sans doute".
characters.B: Accurate and complete in natural English ("I claim that", "the prime"), with the ellipses and subjunctives kept. Two slips: "no doubt" for "sans doute" and "Visibly" for "Visiblement".
characters.C: Complete and well written ("Clearly", "the prime", "[in] addition"). It turns the subjunctive "qui ait les propriétés d'un 2-produit" into "which has the properties", which the footnote then contradicts, and writes "doubtless" for "sans doute".
characters.D: Covers printed page 1 only; there it is error-free, keeping the misprint "par forcément" as "not necessarily" under its comment, the unclosed parenthesis and the doubled "moreover ... moreover". One page says nothing about the diagrams, labels and editors' additions of pages 2-5.
characters.E: Faithful and complete, subjunctives kept ("which should have", "be in"). Its English has calques: "the accent" for the prime and "Visibly", besides "no doubt".
characters.F: Complete, with a neat "[more]over" for the editors' "[en] outre". It completes one ellipsis ("`f_*` being an equivalence"), turns "qui ait" into "which has", and has "Visibly" and "no doubt".
characters.G: The weakest DER version: it leaves "pl. fid." and "pleinement fidèle" in French inside \text in four displays, brackets the whole "moreover" as an editors' addition, drops "d'ailleurs", completes ellipses and turns "qui ait" into "which has". It adds calques ("the index ! (resp. the exponent !)", "of the type exactness") and "quite literally" for "bel et bien".
characters.H: Faithful in content, subjunctives kept. Its English is the most stilted ("equally" for "également" twice, "the accent", "Visibly", "One must besides also find").

DER.conclusion: No version makes a major error. A and B are equivalent for a reader of an edition, with E and H close behind (English calques only: "the accent", "Visibly", "equally"). C, F and G turn the subjunctive "qui ait les propriétés d'un 2-produit" into "which has", which the footnote corrects for the reader; F and G also complete his ellipses. G is the only version that needs repair: French left inside \text in four displays, an editors' bracket widened, a word dropped. Every full version renders "sans doute" as "no doubt" or "doubtless", and five of seven write "Visibly" for "Visiblement".

conclusion: No version makes a major error: all keep the mathematics and the page structure, and only LM D (three marks dropped, words moved across an anchor and into an insertion, \mathrm{Centre} changed, \text{ou} left in French) and DER G (French left in \text labels, an editors' bracket widened) mishandle formulas, marks or brackets in more than one place. The top versions (LM: A, then E, G and H, then F; DER: A and B, then E and H; the one-page versions LM C and DER D are clean on their page) differ by one or two minor slips each, calques such as "effective action", "Visibly" and "the accent" or a smoothed subjunctive, which do not matter to a reader of an edition and fall to a light copy-edit. Only LM D (lost and displaced marks, smoothed syntax) and DER G (untranslated labels, completed ellipses, a dropped word) would need real repair, and the slips shared by most versions ("no doubt" for "sans doute", "effective action" for "action effective") are worth adding to the briefs.
